results.pick_reason: In the picture, A answers both halves of his question: fewer tiers, and even ones. It shows three tiers where today shows five steps (foot band, clamp ring, collar lip, crown and cap: 46, 25, 14, 55 and 68 px on the sheet's crop). Each of A's tiers is 56 px tall (11.3 mm), each step is 12 mm per side, and its sloped foot (46 px) is shorter than a tier, so it reads as the foot. B's four tiers are just as even (42 px, 8.5 mm, 12 mm per side), but its foot is as tall as a tier, so the eye counts five bands, the same as today. The cost of A is a top about 12 % heavier from the side (cap 56 across against 40); B keeps today's weight and is the fallback if he prefers finer steps. Both are rendered fairly and neither reads fake.
results.owner_summary: The new sheet is a fair side-by-side: the same camera, light and backdrop for all three, and the sizes printed match the drawings. A answers both halves of your question: three tiers instead of the five steps you see on today's top, all the same height, each 24 mm narrower than the one below. B's four tiers are just as even, but its sloped foot is as tall as a tier, so it still reads as five; I'd pick A, knowing its top looks a little heavier (the cap is 56 mm across instead of 40).

findings.claim: The lamp as committed still cannot have its shade taken off by hand. The fix (a Ø62 disc on the fixture plus a Ø95/Ø63 white ring on the shade) is drawn and it works, but it is a switch that is off by default. The main build (V3), its meshes and its BOM still carry the Ø95 disc that traps the shade. Whichever top is chosen, the split has to be switched on in the main build, and PARTICULARS' 'Swap by hand, no tools' is untrue until it is.

findings.claim: The new white ring passes the Ø62 hub and disc with only 0.5 mm all round, and that is too tight for a shade moved by hand. The PEEK centering land lets the shade tilt about 1.7-2.3°. About 31-33 mm below the land, that tilt moves the ring roughly 1.0-1.3 mm sideways, so its edge can land on the disc's edge when a shade is lowered off or pushed on. Powder coat on both edges and a hand-placed ring with nothing to locate it make the gap smaller still. The ring is bonded on and sticks 9.5 mm inward from the bond line, so a knock loads the bond in peel. Suggested fixes: turn the ring as part of the collar, with a chamfered, concentric lip, or open the gap to about 1-1.5 mm, which makes a wider dark ring under the hub.
findings.evidence: From the meshes: white-ring.stl r 31.5-47.5, z 63-64. white-disc.stl (A/B) r 8.2-31.0, z 59-60. hub.stl r 31.0. ring.stl (PEEK) r 40.8, z 86-100. findings.claim: The shoulder that used to bottom is gone, and the clamp ring now meets nothing but the silicone. The claim of 'about 4 [mm] of thread below it for travel' does not fit the drawn clamp, though. Its Ø96 thread bore runs through the band down to z 88.87, not only from the ring's foot at 92. Only about 0.1 mm (to the gasket) to 1.3 mm (to the shell) of collar lies between the clamp's lowest thread and the acrylic's crown hole. The end of the collar's thread is not drawn. If the thread runs out at the gasket, the clamp jams after about 0.1 mm, before it squeezes the silicone. The drawing needs an undercut on the collar at about z 86.5-88.8, or a relieved bore in the band so that only the ring is threaded (then about 3 mm of travel to the gasket). Threads are not modelled.

findings.claim: The cord grip fits as drawn, but it is a generic shape, not a real part. The drawn grip has 8 mm of thread and a hex 4 mm and dome 7 mm tall, so 11 mm above its seat. It sits in a Ø22 pocket (not Ø20) with 2.5 mm round the hex corners, 2.0 mm round the dome and 1.0 mm under the 1.5 mm lid. No part is named. Many nylon M12x1.5 dome glands I know of stand roughly 15-20 mm above their seat (UNVERIFIED). The grip cannot sit any lower, because its thread already starts 0.5 mm above the hub's neck. A taller real part would therefore raise the cap and break the even tiers. The cord's size is also not given: the model's Ø6 cord sits near the top of the 3-6.5 range (UNVERIFIED for a braided 18/2 SVT).

It tests the turn only at 30°, lowers in 2 mm steps and then jumps to -30, -60, -100 and -140, ignores overlaps under 1 mm³, uses nominal sizes and does not allow for tilt. It also takes the pins' bottom as z 90.5, so the note's 'lowered to come off' figures of 12.8 and 10.0 should be 12.3 and 9.5 (today 9.0, as the note itself says).

findings.claim: The tapered band's strength figures are plausible and make no practical difference. A simple beam model gives the lane's numbers exactly: 0.113 µm for today's 5 mm band, 0.240 µm tapered from 5 to 1, and a 2.16 MPa peak at the root. Measured along the sphere (a 7.2 mm overhang) they become 0.23/0.50 µm and 3.1 MPa, still far below 6061's yield and far below the silicone's squeeze. The 1.0 mm land and the 54.7° cone are plain lathe work. The face on the silicone is unchanged. The 0.5 MPa load case implies about 1.6 kN of preload, and nothing says the maker's torque delivers that (pre-existing).

Taper code is at crystal.py lines 291-299. The comment at lines 204-206 and top-redraw.md lines 27-28 give the claim. The gasket annulus is r 48.2-58 (gaskets.stl).

findings.claim: The heat numbers reproduce exactly but do not separate the options. In a 35 C room the hub runs 50.6 (today), 50.3 (A) and 50.2 (B). B shows the coolest even though it has the least surface (9,513 mm², against today's 9,676 and A's 9,867). That is because the formula starts each 8.5 mm tier as a fresh cooling surface. Counting the stack's sides as one surface puts B at or below A. Everything is within about 0.5 K and every input is an estimate. No LED or board temperature is computed (UNVERIFIED).

findings.claim: This one predates the redraw and is unchanged by it. The clamp squeezes the shade through two 1 mm air gaps between the three acrylic layers at the crown. The silicone rings are only outside the shell and inside the skin. So 'the acrylic clamped between two silicone rings' depends on the layers bending about 2 mm together, or on spacers that are not drawn. This also decides how much clamp travel M3 must allow.

findings.claim: Every new part can be turned, laser-cut or bought, but A and B have no BOM, cutlist or cost. A's Ø56 cap is wider than the Ø50 cap stock listed. Every shade's metal changes. missed: Grip height could undo the even tiers. The drawn grip stands 11 mm above its seat (crystal.py 219), in a 12 mm pocket (112.5-124.5), and it cannot drop because the hub's neck tops out at 104.0. Standard M12x1.5 polyamide glands stand about 22 mm: Lapp's SKINTOP ST-M XL datasheet (DB53010000EN) gives 37.5 overall less a 15 thread, and Rittal SZ 2411.601 lists height 22 with an 8 thread. Fitting one would add up to about 10 mm to A's and B's tops, so they would no longer be even. M4 leaves this as UNVERIFIED '15-20', and the owner summary says only 'may be taller'. A named low-profile grip should be settled before the owner chooses between A and B.

The 'collar flush, 0.5 proud' look in A and B, and the clamp tier's height, are not controlled. The collar is located by its flange under the skin; the clamp ring sits on the shell through the outer gasket. So the ring's height on the collar follows the whole acrylic stack at the crown: skin 3, gap 1, liner 6, gap 1, shell 3, plus two 1 mm silicone rings (crystal.py 181, 229-234, 281-283). README 1116 says those gaps exist 'because formed parts don't nest perfectly'. At the band's roughly 32° slope, each mm of stack moves the ring about 1.2 mm. If the clamp closes the two air gaps (M10), the ring drops about 2.4 mm and the collar stands about 3 mm proud, recreating today's 'collar lip' step that the redraw removes. The stack needs a datum and a tolerance before the sheet's even heights can be promised.
